helpSubtitle.message: Detailed guides and troubleshooting for BatchShot

helpQuickStartContent.message:
BatchShot supports four efficient capture and execution workflows to meet diverse needs, from single-page archiving to large-scale automated audits:
  • Capture Current Page : Instantly capture and stitch the full length of your active tab. Floating headers are hidden automatically to ensure a clean, timestamped record.
  • Capture Current Window : Automatically cycle through and capture all open tabs in your current window—ideal for comparing multiple referenced pages. If these tabs were previously opened in batch using the "Only Open Links" feature, the capture will automatically inherit and use the original job context (such as {keyword} and {index}) so screenshots are correctly named, watermarked, or reported.
  • Only Open Links : Import and open URLs in the background or new tabs without capturing. This allows you to manually log in, handle CAPTCHAs, or perform setup before capture.
  • Batch Automated Capture : Includes URL List, URL Template, CSS Selector Search, and Sequential Click modes—engineered for high-volume, automated workflows.

Tip: Browser-internal pages (e.g., chrome:// pages), the Chrome Web Store, and local privileged files cannot be captured due to browser extension security restrictions. We recommend configuring shortcuts for 'Capture Current Page' and 'Capture Current Window' in settings for even faster trigger times.

helpUrlListScenario.message: Best for: When you already have an explicit list of URL links (e.g. competitor landing pages, documents, test cases).

helpUrlListContent.message:
• 1. Enter one page URL per line in URLs. Addresses without a protocol are normalized to https://.
  • 2. You can also click Extract Links to collect links from the active page, then filter them by host, title, or address in the Link Selector.
  • 3. Choose the capture mode, format, delay, and folder, then start the task. If reports are enabled, every URL result is written to the report.
  • 4. Use the history button next to the input to restore, pin, rename, or delete previous URL lists.
https://example.com
example.org/pricing
https://docs.example.com/help

Tip: For large batches, test a few URLs first to confirm delay, format, and filename patterns before running the full list.

helpTemplateScenario.message: Best for: Capturing bulk pages where only one or two variables (like IDs, query keywords, cities, page numbers) change in the URL.

helpTemplateContent.message:
• 1. Add one or more URL templates containing %s. Each %s is replaced with the current text-list line.
  • 2. In Text List, enter one keyword, product ID, city, page number, or other variable per line. BatchShot generates tasks from every line.
  • 3. Template mode can mix normal URL templates and CSS selector search templates. The preview shows the task count before you start.
  • 4. Folders, filenames, metadata overlays, and reports can use {keyword} so each screenshot remains traceable to its source text.
https://example.com/search?q=%s
https://example.com/product/%s

camera
tripod

Note: If a single template line contains multiple %s placeholders, they all use the same text value. Use multi-field CSS selector search templates when each field needs a different value.

helpSelectorSearchScenario.message: Best for: When a site doesn't support searching by URL query params and requires you to fill in an input box and click a button or press Enter.

helpSelectorSearchContent.message:
• 1. The basic form is Start URL :: input selector. If the site requires a click, append :: button selector (the default delimiter is :: and can be customized via 'Template search delimiter' in Settings).
  • 2. The text list usually contains one search term per line. If the template contains multiple input selectors, provide multiple fields per line, separated by tabs or the configured template search delimiter.
  • 3. The submit button is optional. Without a button selector, BatchShot fills the fields and presses Enter; with one, it clicks the button.
  • 4. The start URL, inputs, and button must be reachable in the same page context. Cross-origin iframes, closed Shadow DOM, CAPTCHAs, and complex multi-step login flows cannot be automated reliably.
  • 5. Right-click shortcut: Instead of inspecting the DOM manually, you can also right-click the search input on the target page and select "Add search box to BatchShot template". The extension will automatically extract the selector and populate the template.
https://example.com :: input[name="q"]
https://example.com :: input.search :: button[type="submit"]
https://example.com/advanced :: input[name="city"] :: input[name="keyword"] :: button.search

Selector advice: Prefer stable attributes such as input[name="q"] or [data-testid="search"]. Long generated CSS paths are fragile when the page changes.

helpSequentialScenario.message: Best for: Paged lists, continuous articles, or paginated search results where you want to click a 'Next Page' button recursively and screenshot each page.

helpSequentialContent.message:
• 1. Enter the Page URL, Next page CSS selector, and number of Pages. The first page is included, so 3 pages means the current page plus two next clicks.
  • 2. Click Fill from current page to let BatchShot infer the current URL and next button, or click Pick next page and select the next button directly on the page.
  • 3. Once started, BatchShot captures the current page, clicks next, waits for the page to change, and repeats until the target count is reached or the next page is unavailable.
  • 4. You can also use Open links only to prepare sequential pages, verify them manually, then capture the current window.
  • 5. Right-click shortcut: You can also right-click the next page button on the target page and select "Set as next page button for sequential capture" to auto-populate the selector.

Limits: Sequential mode works best with real pagination buttons or links. Infinite scrolling, virtual lists, CAPTCHAs, and multi-step interactions are better handled as URL lists or manually prepared tabs.

helpFilenameFolderScenario.message: Best for: Automatically organizing screenshots into folders or renaming them according to specific conventions.

helpFilenameFolderContent.message: Folder and filename templates can be configured in Settings. Folder: Use / to create nested directories. Filename: Defines the naming format of screenshots. For both fields, you can click the Token Picker below the input box to directly choose and insert variables (such as index, total, host, title, keyword, datetime, etc.) without manually typing them. Filename sanitization is performed automatically.

helpCaptureOutputScenario.message: Best for: Choosing Full Page for long pages, Viewport for visible screen space, PNG/JPG/PDF formats.

helpCaptureOutputContent.message:
• Full page: Scrolls the page in segments, captures each viewport, and stitches the result into one long image. BatchShot tries to hide fixed/sticky elements to reduce repeated headers.
  • Viewport: Captures only the currently visible browser area. Use it for modals, dashboards, and pages where fixed headers must stay visible.
  • PNG: Lossless and usually larger; best for archival and crisp text.
  • JPG: Smaller files with adjustable compression; useful for large visual batches.
  • PDF: Writes the screenshot into a PDF. The quality setting applies here too.
  • Delay: Seconds to wait after load. Search results, lazy images, animations, and async tables often need 2-5 seconds.

helpMetadataScenario.message: Best for: Auditing, forensic evidence, or test logs where screenshot integrity is critical and source info must be hardcoded on the image.

helpMetadataContent.message: When 'Add metadata to image' is enabled, an overlay band is appended to the top or bottom of screenshots. You can click the Token Picker below the inputs to select and arrange the fields (such as capturedAt, url, title, host, index, etc.) you want to display, and customize the font size, colors, padding, and layout in the settings.

helpReportScenario.message: Best for: Auditing and reviewing large-scale batch tasks with an Excel / CSV manifest sheet of results and paths.

helpReportContent.message:
When Export screenshot report is enabled, BatchShot downloads a CSV or XLSX report after the batch finishes. You can click the Token Picker below the fields input in Settings to customize the columns and their order. XLSX format reports automatically preserve clickable hyperlinks.

Save directory: If folder templates place screenshots into different subfolders, the report is saved to their lowest common parent folder.

helpPageTextScenario.message: Scenario: Save searchable page text alongside screenshots for review, archiving, full-text retrieval, or AI analysis.

helpPageTextContent.message:
Enable Page Text Extraction to save the page's visible text and metadata while each screenshot is captured.
How it works:
  • Extraction source: Text comes from the page's visible body text. It is not OCR from the screenshot image, and does not bypass security or login restrictions.
  • Separate text files: Saves a .txt file for each page, named matching the screenshot and saved in the same folder.
  • Combined text file: Exports a single merged .txt file at the end, joining pages with the configured separator.
  • Maximum length: Caps the saved text length per page to avoid oversized files.
  • Export text template: Supports customizing the text output format. You can click the Token Picker below the template box to insert parameters like text body, url, title, capturedAt, etc.
  • Report fields: Enabling report inclusion appends text filename, text length, excerpt, and meta description columns to the report.

Limitations: Internal browser pages, restricted pages, inaccessible frames, or elements rendered with significant delays may result in empty or incomplete text. Use Only Open Links first if manual setup is needed.

helpRuntimeDashboardContent.message:
• Task dashboard: When a batch, template, sequential, or current-window capture starts, the popup shows a task dashboard with progress, completed count, and per-page logs.
  • Pause and resume : While a task is running, use the pause control to temporarily stop queue advancement, then resume after checking page state, login, or network conditions.
  • Stop a task : Clicking the stop button requests cancellation of the current batch. Screenshots that have already downloaded are kept; pending or in-progress items stop advancing.
  • Failure history and reports : After a failure or stopped task, failed items remain traceable through failure history, the dashboard status, or exported reports, making later retries and review easier.
  • Completion and cleanup: After a task completes, fails, or is stopped, the dashboard keeps the final result so you can review successful captures, failure reasons, and downloaded reports before closing it or starting another task.

Tip: Stop is a best-effort request to halt the queue. It may not interrupt a single screenshot or download that is already being exported; that step may finish before later tasks are skipped.

helpScheduledTasksContent.message:
• 1. Enable Enable scheduled captures in the settings first.
  • 2. Set up your capture task in the popup, then click the Clock (Schedule) icon in the footer.
  • 3. Set the target run time and a task name, then click save.
  • 4. Capture schedules rely on background Alarms.

Important Note: Ensure the browser is not fully shut down when the task triggers. System sleep/hibernation might delay or prevent scheduled captures.

helpAutomationScenario.message: Scenario: Notify a local script, business system, or automation workflow after a capture batch finishes.

helpAutomationContent.message:
When Completion Webhook is enabled, BatchShot sends an HTTP request to the configured URL after the current batch ends.
Configuration:
  • Trigger condition: Always, all successful, any failed, or completed without user cancellation.
  • Method: Supports POST and GET.
  • Headers: Enter a JSON object, for example {"Authorization":"Bearer token"}.
  • Body template: Supports {runId}, {taskName}, {status}, {startedAt}, {finishedAt}, {durationMs}, {total}, {success}, {failed}, {cancelled}, {folder}, {reportFilename}, {unfinishedTasksCount}, and {items}.
  • Ignore errors: If enabled, webhook failure will not fail the capture task. If disabled, webhook failure marks the task as failed.
  • Test request: Use the settings page test button to verify the URL, headers, and template.

Webhook sends task summaries and per-page capture results. It does not upload screenshot files by itself.

helpHistoryFailureHistoryContent.message:
• Input history: URL lists, URL templates, text lists, sequential start URLs, and next-page selectors keep recent records. You can pin , rename , delete , or clear them; the history limit is controlled in Settings.
  • Failure history: Failed items from batch tasks appear in the failure panel with their URL, title, error message, and original task context.
  • Retry All: Click Retry All to repack only failed items into a new task. You can also retry or delete single items from the failure list.
  • Reports: When reports are enabled, failure reasons are also written to CSV/XLSX for offline review.

helpShortcutsContent.message:
The extension has these default shortcuts:
  • Alt+Shift+B - Open / toggle the BatchShot popup window
  • Alt+Shift+S - Capture the current active page (Full page)
  • Alt+Shift+W - Capture all tabs in the active window
To rebind or clear these, go to Settings -> Shortcuts and click Edit in Chrome to open Chrome's keyboard shortcuts settings page.

helpTroubleshootingContent.message:
1. Why do some pages fail to capture?

Browsers block extensions from capturing chrome:// pages, the Chrome Web Store, extension pages, and some privileged local pages. For normal websites, failures are usually caused by login state, network timeouts, unfinished loading, or server access rules. Use Open links only first when you need to confirm page state.

2. What should I do when Full page stitching repeats or misses headers?

Full page capture relies on scrolling and stitching. BatchShot temporarily hides fixed/sticky elements, but complex layouts may still misbehave. Try increasing Delay, switching to Viewport, or manually placing the page in a stable state first.

3. Why does CSS selector search fail to submit?

Check that selectors are unique, the elements are not inside an inaccessible iframe or Shadow DOM, and the button is actually clickable. If results update asynchronously, increase Delay. For multi-field templates, make sure each text-list row has the expected number of fields.

4. Why are images blank or table data missing?

This is usually lazy loading, animation, or Ajax data still in progress. Increase Delay to 2-5 seconds. For pages that need login or manual filters, open the batch first, verify the tabs, then capture the current window.

5. Why did a scheduled task not run exactly on time?

Scheduled captures rely on the browser's background Alarm. If the browser is fully closed, the system sleeps, the network is unavailable, or another task is already running, the task may be delayed or skipped. Leave review time for important scheduled jobs.

6. Does Retry All overwrite successful screenshots?

No. Retry All only creates a new task from failed items. Successful captures are not re-downloaded. If filename collisions worry you, include {datetime} in filenames or change the download folder.

helpCopyrightContent.message:
BatchShot is a webpage screenshot and local archiving tool. When you capture webpages, images, text, trademarks, interfaces, or other third-party content, copyright, trademark, and other rights remain with their original owners.

You are responsible for confirming that capturing, saving, distributing, displaying, commercial use, or republication complies with the target site terms, copyright law, privacy rules, and applicable regulations. BatchShot does not upload screenshots to a remote server and does not grant additional rights to third-party content.
